correctness.rationale: The finite chain ring valuation criterion xy=0 iff nu(x)+nu(y)>=ell gives low independent L and high clique H with block A=[[0,B],[B^T,J-I]]. Ideal cardinalities yield B*1_H=-1_L, BB^T=-J_L and |H|=-1 modulo prime p. Solving kernel equations for (z,y): y=B^T z + T1, low forces s+T=0, high-coordinate sum 2T=-s; hence T=s=0 in every characteristic, including p=2. Kernel=(z,B^T z) with sum z=0, so rowspace=(t1_L-By,y), rank |H|+1. Each low valuation layer has cardinality divisible by p, so restricted code dot product is y.y', yielding one-dimensional hull. Constant B-columns occur at the socle and (if ell even) the middle layer; they and only they give singleton codewords and d(C)=1. Equal-valuation low differences prove d(C-dual)=2. Independent direct ring example F3[u]/(u^4) has n=26 rank=9, as asserted; finite equal-characteristic tests do not replace the chain-ring proof.

evidence: Earlier graph papers give real spectra/valuation graph structure, and one special case modular code. They do not state a general prime-field adjacency rowspace across mixed-characteristic chain rings.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The graph structure is an input, not sufficient as a statement of all code/hull/weight-one invariants; length-four special case cannot logically dominate every ell.

evidence: Current C admits e_v for socle v, hence minimum distance one. Prior 2026 Theorem 4.6 asserts d=2 for same special-case simple graph, so the previous statement cannot imply the new correct parameter triple.
Current theorem includes complete dual and exact A_1(C)=(p-1)(q-1)(1+1_even_ell*q^(ell/2-1)), which are beyond the length-four parameter/hull assertions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior agrees on rank/hull but not on d=1 nor the full family and weight-one spectrum. The result genuinely corrects and extends the literature rather than merely renaming it.

evidence: Sarkar et al., Thm 4.6-4.7 for ell=4, q=p odd gives dim p^2 and one-dimensional hull; also reports minimum distance 2.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This paper concerns exactly the same adjacency code in a restricted family, but its d=2 claim fails for the simple adjacency graph due to nonzero socle e_v in its rowspace. It does not give the uniform theorem.

evidence: The exact ell=4 p-odd dimension and hull are known; the d=1 unit-word contradiction is checked by the explicit formula t=1,y=e_v at socle.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No prior table found for all ell>=3, q=p^f and characteristic; this is a uniform structural theorem not a recomputed single table.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Sarkar–Hansda–Maji paper studies the specific F_p[x]/(x^4) graph for odd prime p, obtaining dimension p^2 and hull 1, which are explicitly preexisting special cases. Its claimed adjacency-code minimum distance two conflicts with an explicit socle-column unit word in the same simple adjacency model; the present uniform result instead gives minimum distance one, prime-field rowspace and dual in all nilpotency lengths ell>=3 and all finite commutative chain rings (including mixed characteristic). The graph valuation description is standard; the new content is exact modular code structure and weight-one classification. Potential prior general modular split-graph code theory is a residual risk.
residual_risks: General modular adjacency-code results for nested/split graphs could imply part of the block-rank structure under different terminology.
The existing paper's minimum-distance mismatch depends on using the same simple zero-diagonal adjacency convention; the reviewed proof explicitly fixes that convention.

value.rationale: The adjacency code of a graph is a canonical linear code, and a whole structural class of finite chain rings is intrinsically motivated. Exact rowspace and dual, hull dimension, both distances and first weight-enumerator coefficient for every ring provide useful algebraic invariants and expose a critical coding-theoretic error-correction limitation. This corrects the claimed positive minimum distance of the closest prior special case and extends to residue prime powers and mixed characteristic; it is more than a small exact instance or a restatement of known graph structure.

limitations: Only finite commutative chain rings with ell>=3; exclude length2 and nonchain rings.
Minimum distance1 means no single-error correction, despite some earlier claims; no full weight enumerator.
residual_risks: General modular adjacency-code results for nested/split graphs could imply part of the block-rank structure under different terminology.
The existing paper's minimum-distance mismatch depends on using the same simple zero-diagonal adjacency convention; the reviewed proof explicitly fixes that convention.
